//: Copy this to ~/.config/llm-review/config.json and edit. NOTE: inside a reviewed repo, only excludes/lenses/budget are honoured from a committed config — provider/model/providers/crossRepo/requirementsFile are read only from the user-level config or the env, because a repo ships its own config to whoever clones it. ALL fields are optional — with no config the tool auto-detects a provider and reviews the one repo.
//provider: Which AI backend to use: "claude" (needs the `claude` CLI + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) or "gemini" (needs the `gemini` CLI + GEMINI_API_KEY). Omit to auto-detect (claude, then gemini). Env override: LLM_REVIEW_PROVIDER.
//model: Model to review with, applied to whichever provider is chosen. Omit to use the provider default (claude → opus, gemini → gemini-2.5-pro). NOTE: a top-level "model" is passed to BOTH providers — if you switch between claude and gemini, set per-provider models under "providers" instead (below) so a claude-only id like "opus" isn't sent to gemini. Env override: LLM_REVIEW_MODEL.
//providers: Optional per-provider overrides — the safe way to pin a strong model per backend. bin = command name, model = model id, extraArgs = extra args inserted before the prompt.
//lenses: MULTI-ENGINE. Setting this OVERRIDES the budget profile's reviewer pairing, so leave it unset unless you mean it (the key below is deliberately commented out). Which reviewers to run over each chunk, in PARALLEL. Each is a focused persona with its own mandate, so one bot's blind spot is covered by another. Default: whatever the budget profile pairs them into (balanced runs two composite reviewers covering all four mandates; minimal runs one). Setting this overrides that. Use ["full"] for a single combined pass (cheaper, shallower). Env override: LLM_REVIEW_LENSES=correctness,security,structure,qa (or 'full').
//multi-provider: When BOTH the `claude` and `gemini` CLIs are installed, the lenses are round-robined across them, so two genuinely different models cross-check the same diff. Nothing to configure — install the second CLI and it is used automatically. Force a single one with LLM_REVIEW_PROVIDER.
//adjudication: After merging, a second engine re-checks every finding against the real code and drops the ones it can refute. Runs automatically when a gate is armed and something would block. Force on/off with LLM_REVIEW_ADJUDICATE=1|0.
//budget: TOKEN CONTROLLER. Profile: "minimal" (haiku, <=2 calls), "balanced" (sonnet, <=4 calls, DEFAULT) or "thorough" (opus, <=8 calls). The profile picks the MODEL TIER, the call ceiling, the reviewer's tool-call allowance and the findings cap. Env override: LLM_REVIEW_BUDGET. Per-repo: git config review.llmBudget <profile>.
//model-pin-warning: Setting "model" here, or providers.<name>.model, OVERRIDES the profile's tier — a pinned "opus" makes every profile bill at the top tier. Leave both unset unless you mean it; the tool warns when a pin overrides a cheaper profile.
//speed: Further env knobs, all optional: REVIEW_MAX_CALLS (hard ceiling), REVIEW_TOOL_BUDGET (Read/Grep calls the reviewer may make), REVIEW_MAX_FINDINGS (output cap), REVIEW_MAX_PROMPT_CHARS (per-call prompt ceiling), REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS (420000 — a killed call is wasted tokens), REVIEW_DEADLINE_MS (1200000), REVIEW_PROSE_CAP (40000 per markdown/txt document), LLM_REVIEW_CONCURRENCY.
//style: YOUR conventions. The numbers below are ILLUSTRATIVE, not recommended — they came from one particular codebase. Yours will differ, which is the point. Run `llm-review --learn-style <dirs> --write` to infer these from code you have already written rather than picking numbers by hand. Read from .editorconfig first, then ~/.config/llm-review/style.json, then here. A STYLE.md in the repo is passed to the reviewer verbatim for rules a schema cannot express. Line-length/indent/trailing-whitespace are checked in CODE (no tokens); the model judges consistency with the surrounding files.

style.//severity: How hard to push. 'low' (default) means style never blocks a commit — a gate that blocks on formatting gets switched off. Set 'medium' and gate at medium to enforce it.

//requirementsFile: Optional path (relative to the repo) to a requirements/spec file. The reviewer verifies the change SATISFIES it and flags anything unmet. Also auto-detected: REQUIREMENTS.md / docs/REQUIREMENTS.md. Env override: LLM_REVIEW_REQUIREMENTS (a path OR inline text).
//excludes: Extra git pathspecs to drop from the diff, on top of the built-in defaults (dist/build/out/coverage/node_modules/vendor, *.min.*, *.map, lockfiles). Use this for generated files specific to your repo. Git pathspec magic: '*' also matches '/'.
//crossRepo: When the repo being reviewed matches `match` (regex on its absolute path), also give the reviewer read-only access to `related` repos and steer it with `hint`. First match wins. Omit entirely for a plain single-repo review. Set contractOnly:true to pull related repos in ONLY when the diff looks contract-relevant (endpoints/params/schema/migrations) — keeps unrelated changes fast and cheap.

crossRepo.hint: CROSS-REPO: this frontend renders data from the api-docs repo and calls the backend. When the diff changes how endpoints/params are resolved, verify against the actual docs and backend contracts; flag mismatches.

CROSS-REPO: money movement. Verify amount/currency/rounding, idempotency (a retry must not double-charge), capture/void/refund state transitions, and that every money-moving endpoint is authorized. Check the ledger service and the API docs stay consistent with this change.
